rest.order.answers.unreadableBody: Any endpoint that takes a JSON body, when the body is not valid JSON or a field has the wrong JSON type, such as `{"productId":"KOPI-ARABIKA-250","quantity":"dua"}`. A number written as a string is accepted (`"2"`). ASP.NET Core refuses the body before the endpoint runs, so nothing was read or changed. `errors` is keyed by the JSON path of the fault and, on every endpoint but the return rejection, also carries `request` for the body as a whole. `traceId` here is the request's trace context, not its `X-Request-Id`.
rest.order.answers.emptyBody: `POST /api/v1/cart/items`, `PUT /api/v1/cart/items/{productId}`, `POST /api/v1/cart/voucher` and `POST /api/v1/orders/checkout`, when the request says `Content-Type: application/json` but carries no body, or the body is `null`. With no `Content-Type` either, the answer is `415`. Send a JSON object.
rest.order.answers.tokenMissing: Any endpoint, when the request carries no `Authorization` header, or one that is not `Bearer <token>` (`Basic …`, or `Bearer` alone). Every endpoint of order needs an access token from identity. The body is empty.
rest.order.answers.tokenExpired: Any endpoint, when the access token's `exp` is more than five minutes in the past (the clock skew order allows). `error_description` gives the expiry in UTC. Exchange the refresh token at identity for a new pair, then repeat the request. The body is empty.
rest.order.answers.tokenInvalid: Any endpoint, when the token is not one identity signed for order: a signature that does not verify, a key identity does not publish, another issuer or audience, an algorithm other than `RS256`, or text that is not a JWT at all. `error_description` names the check that failed when there is a text for it, and is left out otherwise. Do not retry with the same token; sign in again. The body is empty.
rest.order.answers.notAccessToken: Any endpoint, when the token is identity's and valid but is not an access token: a refresh token, or the challenge token of a two-factor sign-in. Send the access token instead. The body is empty.
rest.order.answers.unknownPath: A path under `/api/v1/cart` or `/api/v1/orders` that no endpoint serves, for example an order number where an order's `id` belongs (`GET /api/v1/orders/ORD-20261022-7F3A9C1B`). No token is needed to get this answer, and the body is empty.
rest.order.answers.methodNotAllowed: A path order serves, with a method it does not take there: `GET /api/v1/orders/checkout` answers `Allow: POST`, and `POST /api/v1/orders/{orderId}` answers `Allow: GET`. `Allow` lists the methods the path takes. No token is needed to get this answer, and the body is empty.
rest.order.answers.unsupportedMediaType: Any endpoint that takes a JSON body, when the request has a body but its `Content-Type` is missing or is not JSON (`application/json`, `text/json` or any `application/*+json`). Also when a request to `POST /api/v1/cart/items`, `PUT /api/v1/cart/items/{productId}`, `POST /api/v1/cart/voucher` or `POST /api/v1/orders/checkout` has neither a body nor a `Content-Type`. Send `Content-Type: application/json`. Nothing was read or changed.
rest.order.answers.internal: Any endpoint, when something fails that order did not expect. `traceId` is the request's `X-Request-Id`. Whether any of the request took effect is not known: read the current state before repeating it, and repeat a checkout only with the same `Idempotency-Key`, which cannot charge twice.
rest.order.answers.keysUnavailable: Any endpoint, when the token names a signing key order does not hold yet and order's last attempt to fetch identity's published keys failed. Nothing was done, and the token may well be valid: retry shortly with the same token.
rest.order.getCart.summary: Reads the caller's cart: each line at the catalog price captured when it was added, the voucher code set on the cart, and the subtotal. These prices are an indication only; checkout prices the cart again.
rest.order.getCart.who: Any signed-in principal, whatever its role. The cart is always the caller's own, kept under the token's `sub`.
rest.order.getCart.case.cart: The cart as stored. `subtotal` and every `lineTotal` are computed from `unitPrice` and `quantity`. Money is rupiah as a JSON number. `categoryId` is the catalog category's slug, or `null`.
rest.order.getCart.case.empty: The caller has no cart, or it expired: a cart is kept for 14 days after its last change, and reading it does not extend that. `updatedAt` is the time of this answer.
rest.order.getCart.case.cartUnavailable: Order cannot reach the store that holds carts. Nothing was changed; retry shortly.
rest.order.addCartItem.summary: Adds a product to the caller's cart, or adds to the quantity of a product the cart already holds. The product's title, price, category and merchant are read from catalog at that moment.
rest.order.addCartItem.who: Any signed-in principal, into its own cart. A seller cannot add a product it sells itself.
rest.order.addCartItem.field.productId: The product's SKU in catalog. Required: missing or `null` is refused before the cart is read. An empty or blank SKU is passed on to catalog, which knows no such product (`404`).
rest.order.addCartItem.field.quantity: 1 to 999. Added to the quantity the cart already holds for this SKU, and the line may not exceed 999 in all. Left out, it counts as 0 and is refused.
rest.order.addCartItem.case.added: The product is in catalog with a price in IDR and a merchant, and the caller is not that merchant. A new SKU becomes a new line at the end; a SKU already in the cart gets `quantity` added, and its title, price, category and merchant are refreshed from catalog. The 14 days before the cart expires start again.
rest.order.addCartItem.case.invalid: `productId` is missing or `null`. ASP.NET Core refuses the body before the endpoint runs; the key in `errors` is the property's C# name.
rest.order.addCartItem.case.quantityOutO: `quantity` is below 1 or above 999, or was left out. Checked before catalog is asked.
rest.order.addCartItem.case.notInCatalog: Catalog has no product with this SKU, or refused it as malformed (an empty SKU among them). Nothing was added.
rest.order.addCartItem.case.cartBusy: The cart changed under this edit ten times in a row, because other requests were editing it at the same moment. Nothing was changed; repeating the request is safe.
rest.order.addCartItem.case.noUsablePric: Catalog has the product but no price for it, or a price in a currency other than IDR. `message` says which. Nothing was added.
rest.order.addCartItem.case.noMerchant: Catalog names no merchant for the product, so nobody could be paid for it or ship it. Nothing was added.
rest.order.addCartItem.case.ownProduct: The product is sold by the caller's own account. Nothing was added.
rest.order.addCartItem.case.lineQuantity: The SKU is already in the cart, and adding `quantity` would take the line above 999. `quantity` in the answer is the total the line would have held. Nothing was changed.
rest.order.addCartItem.case.catalogUnava: Catalog did not answer, so the product's price could not be established. Nothing was added; retry shortly.
rest.order.addCartItem.case.cartUnavaila: Order cannot reach the store that holds carts. Nothing was changed; retry shortly.
rest.order.updateCartItem.summary: Sets the quantity of one line in the caller's cart, or removes the line with a quantity of 0.
rest.order.updateCartItem.who: Any signed-in principal, in its own cart.
rest.order.updateCartItem.field.productI: The SKU of a line in the cart, exactly as the cart shows it in `productId`.
rest.order.updateCartItem.field.quantity: 0 to 999. The line's new quantity; 0 removes the line. Left out, it counts as 0, so `{}` removes the line.
rest.order.updateCartItem.case.updated: The line holds `quantity` now, or is gone when it was 0. Catalog is not asked, so the line keeps the title and price it was added with. When the cart has no line with this SKU, nothing is written and the cart comes back as it was.
rest.order.updateCartItem.case.quantityO: `quantity` is below 0 or above 999. Nothing was changed.
rest.order.updateCartItem.case.cartBusy: The cart changed under this edit ten times in a row, because other requests were editing it at the same moment. Nothing was changed; repeating the request is safe.
rest.order.updateCartItem.case.cartUnava: Order cannot reach the store that holds carts. Nothing was changed; retry shortly.
rest.order.removeCartItem.summary: Removes one line from the caller's cart.
rest.order.removeCartItem.who: Any signed-in principal, from its own cart.
rest.order.removeCartItem.field.productI: The SKU of the line to remove, exactly as the cart shows it in `productId`.
rest.order.removeCartItem.case.removed: The line is gone, and the cart is answered without it. When the cart has no line with this SKU, nothing is written and the cart comes back as it was, still with `200`.
rest.order.removeCartItem.case.cartBusy: The cart changed under this edit ten times in a row, because other requests were editing it at the same moment. Nothing was changed; repeating the request is safe.
rest.order.removeCartItem.case.cartUnava: Order cannot reach the store that holds carts. Nothing was changed; retry shortly.
rest.order.applyCartVoucher.summary: Sets the voucher code checkout will offer to pricing for the caller's cart, replacing any code set before.
rest.order.applyCartVoucher.who: Any signed-in principal, on its own cart.
rest.order.applyCartVoucher.field.vouche: Required and not blank, at most 50 characters. Stored as sent. Whether it gives a discount is not checked here: pricing decides that at checkout.
rest.order.applyCartVoucher.case.applied: The code is set on the cart in `appliedVoucherCode`. `subtotal` does not change: the discount, if pricing grants one, appears only on the order.
rest.order.applyCartVoucher.case.codeReq: `voucherCode` is missing, empty or only spaces. To take a code off the cart, use `DELETE /api/v1/cart/voucher`.
rest.order.applyCartVoucher.case.tooLong: `voucherCode` is longer than 50 characters. Nothing was changed.
rest.order.applyCartVoucher.case.cartBus: The cart changed under this edit ten times in a row, because other requests were editing it at the same moment. Nothing was changed; repeating the request is safe.
rest.order.applyCartVoucher.case.cartUna: Order cannot reach the store that holds carts. Nothing was changed; retry shortly.
rest.order.removeCartVoucher.summary: Takes the voucher code off the caller's cart.
rest.order.removeCartVoucher.who: Any signed-in principal, on its own cart.
rest.order.removeCartVoucher.case.remove: `appliedVoucherCode` is `null` now. When no code was set, nothing is written and the cart comes back as it was, still with `200`.
rest.order.removeCartVoucher.case.cartBu: The cart changed under this edit ten times in a row, because other requests were editing it at the same moment. Nothing was changed; repeating the request is safe.
rest.order.removeCartVoucher.case.cartUn: Order cannot reach the store that holds carts. Nothing was changed; retry shortly.
rest.order.clearCart.summary: Deletes the caller's cart: every line and the voucher code.
rest.order.clearCart.who: Any signed-in principal, its own cart.
rest.order.clearCart.case.cleared: The cart is gone, or there was none. The next read answers an empty cart. No body.
rest.order.clearCart.case.cartUnavailabl: Order cannot reach the store that holds carts. Nothing was changed; retry shortly.
rest.order.checkout.summary: Places an order for everything in the caller's cart. Order prices the cart again through catalog and pricing, places the address on the map and quotes shipping, then runs the checkout saga: the voucher, flash-sale stock, warehouse stock, an escrow hold that debits the buyer's Kinetix wallet, and the warehouse's task. A `201` means the order is `PAID` and the wallet has been debited; nothing further is paid.
rest.order.checkout.who: Any signed-in principal, buying for itself: the buyer is the token's `sub`. A seller cannot buy a product it sells itself.
rest.order.checkout.field.idempotencyKey: Any text up to 100 characters, kept per buyer; a fresh UUID for each new checkout is the usual choice. Repeat a request with the same key and the same body to learn what the first attempt became, without any chance of a second charge. The same key with a different body is refused. Without the header, or with a blank one, every request is a new checkout.
rest.order.checkout.field.shippingAddres: Required and not blank, at most 500 characters. Free text that identity places on the map; it has to resolve to at least a suburb, and a street is better.
rest.order.checkout.field.recipientName: Required and not blank, at most 128 characters: the person the courier hands the parcel to.
rest.order.checkout.field.recipientPhone: Required and not blank, at most 32 characters. No format is checked.
rest.order.checkout.field.shippingServic: A tier exactly as the courier service names it, case included: `KINETIX_INSTANT`, `KINETIX_SAMEDAY`, `KINETIX_REGULAR` or `KINETIX_CARGO`. Left out or blank, order takes the cheapest tier that can carry this parcel on this route and that pricing has a rate for.
rest.order.checkout.field.voucherCode: At most 50 characters. Takes the place of the code set on the cart; an empty string checks out with no voucher, and leaving the field out uses the cart's code. A code pricing does not grant is not an error: the order is placed without it and `appliedVoucher` is `null`.
rest.order.checkout.case.placed: Every step of the saga succeeded: the order is `PAID`, the buyer's wallet has been debited and the total is held in escrow until the order completes, the warehouse has its task, and the cart is emptied (should emptying it fail, the order still stands and the cart keeps its lines). Keep `id` to read the order, and `orderNumber`, the number the admin endpoints and the other services use. `Location` is the order's path. Amounts are rupiah: `finalTotal` is `subtotal` minus `discountAmount` plus `finalShippingFee`, and a voucher discounts the goods, never shipping.
rest.order.checkout.case.replayed: The same key and the same body were sent before, and that checkout placed the order. Nothing new is done: the order is answered as it stands now, so `status` may have moved on and `driverPrincipalId` is set once a courier has delivered it. Amounts read back from the database carry two decimals (`202000.00`).
rest.order.checkout.case.recipientRequir: `shippingAddress`, `recipientName` or `recipientPhone` is missing, empty or only spaces; `field` names the first one. These are checked before anything else.
rest.order.checkout.case.tooLong: A value is longer than an order can record; `field` names it and `maxLength` gives the limit: `shippingAddress` 500, `recipientName` 128, `recipientPhone` 32, `voucherCode` 50, and the `Idempotency-Key` header 100.
rest.order.checkout.case.cartEmpty: The caller's cart has no lines, or has expired. Nothing was placed.
rest.order.checkout.case.twoMerchants: The cart holds products of more than one merchant, and an order belongs to one. Remove one merchant's lines, check out, then add them back for a second order.
rest.order.checkout.case.tierUnknown: The courier service has no tier by the name in `shippingServiceTier`. `availableTiers` lists the tiers that can carry this parcel on this route; pick one of them, or leave the field out.
rest.order.checkout.case.notInCatalog: A product in the cart is no longer in catalog. Remove it from the cart and check out again.
rest.order.checkout.case.inProgress: The checkout this key started has not finished yet: its order is still `PENDING_PAYMENT`. Repeat the same request with the same key in a few seconds to learn how it ended. A checkout whose saga finished but that could not record it is marked `PAID` after about five minutes; one that stopped before its saga began is cancelled after 15 minutes.
rest.order.checkout.case.merchantNotTrad: Identity does not let the cart's merchant sell now: the merchant is unknown to it, or its status is neither `verified` nor `active`. Nothing was placed.
rest.order.checkout.case.rolledBack: A step of the saga was refused, and everything earlier steps had reserved or charged has been given back. The order exists as `CANCELLED` under `orderNumber`. `reason` starts with the step that refused it: `voucher:`, `flash sale <id>:`, `stock for <sku>:`, `escrow:` (a wallet balance short of the total among them; top up at payment first) or `fulfilment:`. Change what `reason` names, then check out again with a new `Idempotency-Key`.
rest.order.checkout.case.rollbackPending: Like the case above, but some of what earlier steps had reserved or charged is still being given back. Order keeps retrying that on its own, and staff are alerted if it cannot. The order is `CANCELLED`; a new attempt needs a new `Idempotency-Key`.
rest.order.checkout.case.replayedNotPlac: The same key and the same body were sent before, and that checkout was not placed. `error` and `rolledBack` say whether everything has been given back, as in the two cases above (`CHECKOUT_ROLLED_BACK` or `CHECKOUT_ROLLBACK_PENDING`); `reason` is the first attempt's. A checkout that stopped before its saga began is answered this way too, once it has been cancelled. The key is spent: send a new one.
rest.order.checkout.case.keyReused: This `Idempotency-Key` already belongs to a checkout of this buyer whose body was different. `orderNumber` is that checkout's order. Nothing was done: send a new key, or repeat the first request exactly.
rest.order.checkout.case.pricingRefused: Pricing refused to price the cart as it stands; `reason` is pricing's own text. Nothing was placed.
rest.order.checkout.case.totalZero: Pricing brought the order to a total of 0, and payment cannot hold or charge nothing. Nothing was placed.
rest.order.checkout.case.ownProduct: A product in the cart is sold by the caller's own account. Remove it from the cart and check out again.
rest.order.checkout.case.lineQuantityOut: A line in the cart holds a quantity outside 1 to 999, which only a cart written before these limits existed can do. Change the line with `PUT /api/v1/cart/items/{productId}` and check out again.
rest.order.checkout.case.noMerchant: Catalog names no merchant for a product in the cart. Nothing was placed.
rest.order.checkout.case.noUsablePrice: Catalog has no price for a product in the cart, or a price in a currency other than IDR. Nothing was placed.
rest.order.checkout.case.weightUnknown: Catalog has no weight for the products in `productIds`, so the parcel cannot be weighed and shipping cannot be priced. Nothing was placed; the merchant has to set the weight.
rest.order.checkout.case.storeNotOnMap: Identity has no point on the map for the merchant's store, so the distance cannot be measured. Nothing was placed; the merchant has to complete its store address.
rest.order.checkout.case.addressNotPlace: The shipping address could not be placed precisely enough to deliver to. `reason` is `NOT_FOUND`, `AMBIGUOUS`, `OUT_OF_SERVICE_AREA`, `INSUFFICIENT_ADDRESS` or `TOO_VAGUE` (placed no closer than a city), and `message` says what to add. Nothing was placed; correct `shippingAddress` and check out again.
rest.order.checkout.case.tierNotEstablis: The tier asked for cannot be sold for this order: the courier service cannot carry this parcel on this route with it (`rateCardReason` gives its reason), or pricing has no rate for it. `availableTiers` lists the tiers that can carry it. When no tier was asked for and pricing has a rate for none of them, `requestedTier` is `any`. Nothing was placed.
rest.order.checkout.case.notServiceable: No tier of the courier service can carry this parcel to this address: too far, too heavy, or too light for cargo. `reasons` gives each tier's reason. Nothing was placed.
rest.order.checkout.case.quoteMalformed: The courier service answered with a shipping quote order cannot read. This is a fault in Kinetix, not in the request; it has been logged, and retrying is unlikely to help. Nothing was placed.
rest.order.checkout.case.feeContradicted: Pricing answered with a shipping fee that is not a discount of the quoted fee, so order refused to charge it. This is a fault in Kinetix, not in the request. Nothing was placed.
rest.order.checkout.case.amountsUncharge: Pricing's amounts do not add up to something escrow can hold: a discount larger than the goods, a total that is not the merchant's share plus shipping, a fraction of a minor unit, or lines that do not match the cart. This is a fault in Kinetix, not in the request; retrying is unlikely to help. Nothing was placed.
rest.order.checkout.case.cartUnavailable: Order cannot reach the store that holds carts. Nothing was placed; retry shortly with the same `Idempotency-Key`.
rest.order.checkout.case.catalogUnavaila: Catalog did not answer for a product in the cart. Nothing was placed; retry shortly with the same `Idempotency-Key`.
rest.order.checkout.case.standingUnknown: Identity did not answer whether the cart's merchant may sell. Nothing was placed; retry shortly with the same `Idempotency-Key`.
rest.order.checkout.case.storeAddressUna: Identity did not answer where the merchant's store is. Nothing was placed; retry shortly with the same `Idempotency-Key`.
rest.order.checkout.case.addressLookupUn: The shipping address could not be placed on the map because identity or its geocoder did not answer. Nothing was placed; retry shortly with the same `Idempotency-Key`.
rest.order.checkout.case.shippingUnavail: The courier service did not answer for a shipping quote. Nothing was placed; retry shortly with the same `Idempotency-Key`.
rest.order.checkout.case.pricingUnavaila: Pricing did not answer, either for the shipping rates or for the order's prices. Nothing was placed; retry shortly with the same `Idempotency-Key`.
rest.order.checkout.case.dependencyUnava: A service the saga called did not answer, so the checkout was stopped and unwound. The order exists as `CANCELLED` under `orderNumber`, and `rolledBack` says whether everything has been given back yet; what is left is retried on its own. This key is spent: retry shortly with a new `Idempotency-Key`.
rest.order.listMyOrders.summary: Lists the orders the caller placed as a buyer, newest first, one page at a time.
rest.order.listMyOrders.who: Any signed-in principal. Only orders whose buyer is the token's `sub` are listed; a seller does not see its store's orders here.
rest.order.listMyOrders.field.status: An order status, matched without regard to case: `PENDING_PAYMENT`, `PAID`, `PROCESSING_FULFILLMENT`, `SHIPPED`, `DELIVERED`, `COMPLETED`, `CANCELLED` or `REFUNDED`. No order is ever `SHIPPED` or `REFUNDED`. Left out or empty, every status is listed.
rest.order.listMyOrders.field.page: An integer from 1; 1 when the parameter is left out. Given empty (`page=`), it is refused rather than taken as 1.
rest.order.listMyOrders.field.pageSize: An integer from 1 to 100; 10 when the parameter is left out. Given empty (`pageSize=`), it is refused rather than taken as 10.
rest.order.listMyOrders.case.page: `items` holds up to `pageSize` orders, newest first, in the same shape as checkout's answer; amounts carry two decimals. `totalCount` counts every order that matches `status`, so there are more pages while `page` × `pageSize` is below it.
rest.order.listMyOrders.case.invalid: `page` or `pageSize` is not an integer, or is given empty, in which case the message reads `The value '' is invalid.` ASP.NET Core refuses it before the endpoint runs.
rest.order.listMyOrders.case.statusUnkno: `status` is not one of the order statuses, which `allowedStatuses` lists. A number is not accepted in place of a name.
rest.order.getOrder.who: The buyer who placed the order, or an `admin`. Anyone else is answered as if the order did not exist.
rest.order.getOrder.field.orderId: The order's `id` from checkout or the list: a UUID, not the `orderNumber`. A value that is not a UUID matches no endpoint and is answered `404` with no body.
rest.order.getOrder.case.found: The order in the same shape as checkout's answer, with amounts to two decimals. `driverPrincipalId` is the courier who delivered it, set once delivery is reported, and `null` before.
rest.order.getOrder.case.notFound: No order has this `id`, or the caller is neither its buyer nor an `admin`. The two are answered alike, so the answer does not reveal other buyers' orders.
rest.order.completeOrder.summary: Completes a delivered order now instead of when its return window closes, and releases its escrow to the merchant.
rest.order.completeOrder.case.released: The order was `DELIVERED` with no return open, and is `COMPLETED` now, recorded under the admin's `sub`. Payment released the escrow to the merchant at once.
rest.order.completeOrder.case.releasePen: The order is `COMPLETED`, but payment did not release the escrow on this attempt; `detail` says why. A refusal from payment waits until staff resolve it; payment not answering is retried on its own, at growing intervals of up to an hour. Do not call this endpoint again for it: the order is complete, and a second call answers `409`.
rest.order.completeOrder.case.notAdmin: The token is valid but its role is not `admin`. The body is empty.
rest.order.completeOrder.case.alreadyCom: The order is complete already, by its return window or an earlier call. If its escrow release is still owed, it is retried on its own, unless payment refused it; a refusal waits for staff.
rest.order.completeOrder.case.returnUnre: A return against the order is still `OPEN` or `GOODS_RECEIVED`, so the buyer may yet be owed a refund. Resolve the return first; an `OPEN` one can be rejected with `POST /api/v1/orders/returns/{returnNumber}/reject`.
rest.order.completeOrder.case.notDeliver: The order is not `DELIVERED`; `message` names its status. Only a delivered order can be completed.
rest.order.listReturnsNeedingAttention.s: Lists the returns that wait on a person: those still `OPEN`, and those whose goods came back but whose refund stopped and is not retried on its own. Oldest first.
rest.order.listReturnsNeedingAttention.f: How many returns to answer: an integer, clamped to 1 to 200 rather than refused. 50 when the parameter is left out; given empty (`limit=`), it is refused.
rest.order.listReturnsNeedingAttention.c: The returns, oldest `openedAt` first; an empty array when there are none. An `OPEN` return blocks its order's completion until its goods come back or an admin rejects it. A `GOODS_RECEIVED` one owes the buyer `refundAmount` (rupiah, two decimals), and `lastRefundError` says why it has not been paid.
`limit` is not an integer, or is given empty. ASP.NET Core refuses it before the endpoint runs.
The token is valid but its role is not `admin`. The body is empty.
rest.order.rejectReturn.summary: Rejects an open return whose goods have not come back. The buyer gets no refund, and the order completes when its return window closes, paying the merchant.
rest.order.rejectReturn.who: An `admin` only; the rejection is recorded under the admin's `sub`.
rest.order.rejectReturn.field.reason: Required and not blank: why the return is rejected. Trimmed, and kept to its first 500 characters. A request with no body at all is answered as a missing reason.
rest.order.rejectReturn.case.rejected: The return was `OPEN` with no goods received, and is `REJECTED` now. No body.
rest.order.rejectReturn.case.reasonRequi: `reason` is missing, empty or only spaces. Checked before the return is looked up.
rest.order.rejectReturn.case.notAdmin: The token is valid but its role is not `admin`. The body is empty.
rest.order.rejectReturn.case.alreadyReje: The return was rejected before. Nothing changed.
rest.order.rejectReturn.case.goodsReceiv: The goods came back (the return is `GOODS_RECEIVED` or `RESOLVED`), so the buyer is owed a refund and the return cannot be rejected.
rest.order.listSagasNeedingAttention.sum: Lists the checkout sagas that could not unwind on their own and wait on a person, most recently flagged first, with every step not yet given back and how to give it back by hand.
rest.order.listSagasNeedingAttention.fie: How many sagas to answer: an integer, clamped to 1 to 200 rather than refused. 50 when the parameter is left out; given empty (`limit=`), it is refused.
rest.order.listSagasNeedingAttention.cas: The sagas, newest `needsAttentionAt` first; an empty array when there are none. `state` is `Running`, `Completed`, `Compensating`, `Compensated`, `Stuck` or `Abandoned`; an `Abandoned` saga is not retried any more. Each entry in `unreleasedSteps` is a step not yet given back, or one given back with a concern: its `name` is `RedeemVoucher`, `AllocateFlashSaleStock`, `ReserveStock`, `CreateEscrowHold` or `CreateFulfillmentOrder`, its `state` is `Attempting`, `Done`, `Failed` or `Compensated`, and `remedy` names the call that gives it back. `correlationId` is the `X-Request-Id` of the checkout that started the saga.
`limit` is not an integer, or is given empty. ASP.NET Core refuses it before the endpoint runs.
The token is valid but its role is not `admin`. The body is empty.
rest.order.countSagasNeedingAttention.su: Counts the checkout sagas that wait on a person.
rest.order.countSagasNeedingAttention.ca: The number, as a bare JSON integer: every saga the list above would answer, without its limit.
The token is valid but its role is not `admin`. The body is empty.
